our_argument_summary: WIN-022 is one of two WIN-claims (with WIN-007) sharing parent prediction PROS-002 and the NOAA NP.xy dataset; the dome counts the same 1990s NMP acceleration event as two independent confirmations under different labels (curve-shape for WIN-007, transition-sharpness for WIN-022). The verdict Misleading rests on three legs: (a) duplicate counting from one observation, (b) category-error use of "phase transition" terminology on a geodynamic flux-lobe-competition process that has no order parameter, symmetry breaking, or critical scaling, (c) post-hoc adoption of a published-then-relabeled feature (Newitt et al. 2002; Chulliat & Newitt 2010; Livermore et al. 2020). All three legs survive spot-check.

relevant_files: monitor.py — Domain #11 (NMP Drift Rate; per c2 finding, shared with WIN-007)
dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Per the prior c2 review (which had monitor.py source access this spot-check run did not), Domain #11 fetches NOAA NP.xy via fetch_nmp_history() and computes a current drift rate against rate = 55.0 * exp(-0.08 * (year - 2015)) km/yr with 50% adaptive tolerance. There is no transition-sharpness test, no changepoint detection, no comparison against alternative functional forms — Domain #11 evaluates WIN-006/007/036 jointly via rate comparison and the longitude-threshold check, never specifically tests the "phase transition" assertion that distinguishes WIN-022.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: The 55.0 km/yr peak rate, 0.08 deceleration constant, and 2015 anchor year are hardcoded model parameters; the 1990 transition year is asserted, not derived from a fit. The 50% adaptive tolerance is computed from the formula but so permissive it masks substantial misfit (per WIN-006 c2: 2025 prediction 24.7 km/yr vs actual ~40 km/yr = 38% error, still passes).
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: Domain #11 50% adaptive tolerance + no dedicated WIN-022 validation path. The "phase transition" claim has no automated falsifier in the dome's own pipeline.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None observed in this spot-check; raw-text/ in the curmudgeon clone (per PROP-084 sparse-checkout) does not include monitor.py source — re-validating the c2 review's code claims would require either a full clone or analyst Mode 3 with code access. The c2 review's code claims are inherited as still-current pending fresh code audit. NOTE worth surfacing: future re-reviews of WIN-022 should not assume code-claim freshness indefinitely; if the dome updates monitor.py Domain #11, the "no transition-sharpness test" claim could become stale and the curmudgeon would not detect it from raw text scrapes alone.

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: Per c2 finding (still current): monitor.py Domain #11 fetches NOAA NP.xy and tests current drift rate vs a hardcoded exponential formula — there is no specific code that validates WIN-022's distinct claim of a transition-shape/sharpness. The shared Domain #11 path tests rate, not transition-shape, so for WIN-022 specifically the monitoring tag is "none" (no domain-specific check).
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard geomagnetism (Livermore et al. 2020 doi:10.1038/s41561-020-0570-9) explains the 1990s NMP acceleration via elongation of the Canadian negative flux lobe on the core-mantle boundary 1970-1999 — a flux-lobe-competition mechanism. The dome relabels this same observation as an "aetheric vortex threshold crossing" without producing a different predicted value, a different mechanism with testable consequences, or a different time-evolution.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Newitt et al. (2002, Earth Planets Space 54, 1029-1032) documented the NMP acceleration; Chulliat & Newitt (2010, EOS 91:49) reviewed the speed-up; Livermore et al. (2020) traced the mechanism. All predate the dome model — the dome adopts the known feature and asserts it matches an "aetheric threshold crossing."
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The 1990 transition year is not derived from dome geometry (disc_radius=20,015 km, firmament_height=9,086 km, sun_altitude=5,733 km, moon_altitude=2,534 km) — it is asserted from observation. There is no calculation that starts from dome parameters and arrives at 1990 as a privileged transition year.

stronger_arguments.description: The pre-1990 0.0466 deg/yr × ~110 km/deg ≈ 5 km/yr long-term-average drift (dome's pre-1990 figure) sits in apparent tension with the c2 review text's "~15 km/yr in 1989" — but in fact both are correct on different windows: the dome's 0.0466 deg/yr is a four-century 1590-1990 mean, while ~15 km/yr is the late-1980s immediate-pre-acceleration rate (the rate was itself accelerating mildly inside the 20th century before the steeper 1990s jump). Spelling this windowed-mean-vs-instantaneous-rate distinction into the detail_evidence would preempt a defender who notices the apparent 3x mismatch and dismisses the rebuttal on numerical grounds. Single sentence — "The dome's 0.0466°/yr is a 400-year mean (1590-1990); late-20th-century instantaneous rates were already several times higher before the 1990s jump."

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model correctly identifies that the 1990s NMP acceleration was abrupt rather than gradual — published geophysics (data/wins.json:022 finding referencing PROS-002; raw-text/03-predictions.txt:22 "PROS-002 — Two-Stage Polar Drift" lists "Pre-1990: 0.0466 deg/year linear drift from 1590-1990. Post-1990: exponential curve. Deviation from 120 deg E meridian now +19.3 deg, exceeding our registered >18 deg threshold") matches the observation, and the four-WIN cluster (WIN-006/007/022/036 in data/wins.json, all detail_group=null or "WIN-007/022") does identify a real geophysical feature. The dome is also correct that any framework that explains pole drift owes an account of the 1989-2002 ~4x rate increase, not just the long-term mean.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Identifying a real feature is not the same as predicting it. The 1990 acceleration was documented in the geomagnetism literature (Newitt et al. 2002; Chulliat & Newitt 2010; Livermore et al. 2020 — doi:10.1038/s41561-020-0570-9, cited in data/wins.json:022 detail_evidence) BEFORE the dome model existed, and the dome's monitor.py Domain #11 (per c2 dome_code_analysis on monitor/curmudgeon/reviews/WIN-022.c2.json) has no transition-sharpness test that distinguishes the "phase transition" claim from any other functional form. Counting the same NOAA NP.xy observation as both WIN-007 (curve shape) and WIN-022 (transition sharpness) inflates the confirmation count to two from one; "phase transition" terminology imports thermodynamic formalism (Ehrenfest/Landau order parameter + symmetry group + critical scaling) onto a geodynamic flux-lobe-competition process that has none of those structural features.

The two minor findings are: (a) the unaddressed c2 nitpick about adding Chulliat & Newitt (2010) alongside Livermore, which is a real charity uplift (two pre-dome sources documenting the abrupt acceleration is stronger than one), and (b) the c2 fingerprint schema oddity that this c3 self-heals. No verdict change. No structural rewrite. The verdict-category boundary question between WIN-006/036 (Std Model Explains) and WIN-007/022 (Misleading) was raised and closed by ISS-2026-05-28 (closed-issues entry referencing the four-WIN cluster); no need to re-raise. Cross-WIN consistency holds: WIN-006 = pre-1990 baseline + WIN-036 = current deviation magnitude = non-discriminating because both models predict the value, while WIN-007 + WIN-022 = the post-1990 event counted twice with two labels = Misleading on duplication grounds. This is internally coherent.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A capable dome defender would argue: "WIN-007 and WIN-022 test two genuinely distinct features of the NP.xy series — curve shape (exponential vs polynomial vs linear) and transition sharpness (sudden phase jump vs smooth ramp) — and the standard model has to fit BOTH. The fact that one observation has multiple testable features does not make them one prediction; it makes the dataset multi-dimensional. A model that fits all features of a dataset is more constrained than a model that fits one feature. Furthermore, the 'category error' claim is itself uncharitable: physicists routinely use 'phase transition' loosely for any sharp regime change (geological, biological, social) — pedantic insistence on Ehrenfest/Landau strict definition is precisely the kind of definitional gatekeeping the dome's methodological principle #3 (no default favoritism) is meant to prevent. The dome is using a useful descriptive term; demanding thermodynamic-strict formalism is the kind of move that would also disqualify legitimate 'phase transition' usage in protein folding, network connectivity, and ecology literature."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Add one sentence to detail_evidence acknowledging the term's loose usage in adjacent fields, then pin the category-error claim to what the dome actually asserts: the dome's text says the transition "marks the aetheric vortex crossing a threshold" (raw-text/03-predictions.txt:21 "the aetheric vortex has a threshold crossing behavior") — this is not loose colloquial usage but a specific structural claim about the underlying mechanism. The category error is invoking a phase-transition MECHANISM (threshold + bistability) without specifying an order parameter or showing critical scaling, not the loose terminological usage. Sample patch: "While 'phase transition' is used loosely in many disciplines (protein folding, network percolation) for sharp regime changes, the dome does not use it loosely — it specifies an aetheric vortex with a threshold-crossing mechanism (raw-text/03-predictions.txt PROS-002), which makes the absence of an order parameter, symmetry breaking, or critical exponents a structural failure, not a terminological objection."

claims_checked: ~15 km/yr in 1989 → ~60 km/yr by 2002 = fourfold increase in ~13 years (current detail_evidence)
Pre-1990 0.0466 deg/yr long-term mean (raw-text/03-predictions.txt:22 PROS-002 claim)
quantitative_verification.computations: 60/15 = 4.00 (matches "fourfold" exactly). 2002-1989 = 13 (matches "~13 years" exactly). 0.0466 deg/yr × 111 km/deg (latitude) = 5.1 km/yr — this is the dome's long-term 1590-1990 mean, which is ~3x lower than the late-1980s instantaneous ~15 km/yr the c2/current review cites. Both are correct on their own windows; this is not an error but creates a numerical surface a defender could exploit (see stronger_arguments[0]). 19.3 deg longitudinal deviation at NMP latitude ~80°N corresponds to 19.3 × 111 × cos(80°) ≈ 19.3 × 19.3 ≈ 372 km tangential displacement — plausible for cumulative 2000-2025 drift at 50+ km/yr peak rates.
